{"id": "463b4f6896ab47719c885f00db53e4fe", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Fast agent report: a separate fast agent investigated this same incident in parallel and has finished. This is its whole final report, shared once. Nobody has checked it.

## Root cause
The ReleaseOrchestrator failure doesn't start in the orchestrator itself. It comes from the nested runbook it calls. The orchestrator's executeAutomation step starts a child execution of the ApplyAppConfig runbook. That runbook runs an aws:runCommand step (AWS-RunShellScript) on the target EC2 instance i-00000000000000001_47. The shell script prints "applying release configuration", finds that /etc/app/app.conf isn't on the instance, and exits with status 3. That fails the leaf runbook, and the orchestrator then fails with "Failed to run automation with executionId ... Failed". The root cause is that the configuration file the release step needs is missing on the managed instance. The cause is not the automation logic, IAM or SSM. The same failure has repeated on every ReleaseOrchestrator run in us-east-1: 2026-11-14 13:28, and 2026-11-25 at 03:46, 05:34 and 07:18 UTC. Every run failed the same way with ResponseCode 3, so this is a persistent precondition failure on the instance, not a transient one.
## Evidence
- ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions: ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ReleaseOrchestrator (00000000-0000-4000-8000-a6cfcc6a3c07, start 2026-11-25T07:18:43Z) Failed: "Failed to run automation with executionId: 00000000-0000-4000-8000-5ec9f0350679 Failed".
- ssm:DescribeAutomationExecutions: child ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ApplyAppConfig (c40fd382-..., ParentAutomationExecutionId=5f5732bd-..., start 07:18:49Z) Failed while verifying command 00000000-0000-4000-8000-9c09aa25f432: Status=Failed, ResponseCode=3, "config file /etc/app/app.conf missing".
- ssm:ListCommandInvocations 34938b01-...: AWS-RunShellScript on i-00000000000000001_47, plugin aws:runShellScript rc=3, output "applying release configuration ... config file /etc/app/app.conf missing / failed to run commands: exit status 3".
- Same parent→child→rc=3 "/etc/app/app.conf missing" pattern in earlier ReleaseOrchestrator runs: aebf62ab-... (2026-11-25T03:46Z), cdd22328-... (05:34Z) and the ApplyAppConfig child f7647ed3-... (2026-11-14T13:28Z).
## Affected resources
- ReleaseOrchestrator runbook (ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator)
- ApplyAppConfig child runbook (ssm-baseline-m4-*-ApplyAppConfig)
- EC2 instance i-00000000000000001_47 (/etc/app/app.conf missing)
- SSM command 00000000-0000-4000-8000-9c09aa25f432
## Gaps
- I couldn't find execution ID 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab in us-east-1: DescribeAutomationExecutions returned nothing and DescribeAutomationStepExecutions returned NotFound. I also had no ssm:GetAutomationExecution permission. My analysis instead uses the matching ReleaseOrchestrator executions found in the account, which all fail the same way.
- I didn't find out why /etc/app/app.conf is missing on the instance (never provisioned, deleted, or a wrong path in the script).", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

", "signature": "", "type": "thinking"}, {"text": "The ReleaseOrchestrator run failed because its nested ApplyAppConfig runbook ran a shell script on the target instance that requires `/etc/app/app.conf`. That file wasn't on the instance, so the script exited with code 3. Nothing in the orchestrator itself broke.

One caveat first: I couldn't find execution `0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab` in account 012345678901_1, us-east-1. Searching by that ID returned nothing, and looking up its steps said it doesn't exist. I also don't have the `ssm:GetAutomationExecution` permission. So I analysed the most recent matching run, `00000000-0000-4000-8000-a6cfcc6a3c07` (`ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ReleaseOrchestrator`, 2026-11-25 07:18:43 UTC).

**How the failure moved up the chain**
1. **Orchestrator:** step `Prepare` (a 5-second sleep) succeeded. Step `RunApplyConfig` then started the child runbook `ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ApplyAppConfig` (execution `c40fd382-…`) for instance `i-00000000000000001_47`.
2. **Child runbook:** its step `ApplyConfig` ran a shell script on the instance through Run Command (command `00000000-0000-4000-8000-9c09aa25f432`):
   ```
   echo "applying release configuration"
   if [ ! -f /etc/app/app.conf ]; then echo "config file /etc/app/app.conf missing" >&2; exit 3; fi
   echo "configuration applied"
   ```
3. **On the instance:** the script printed `config file /etc/app/app.conf missing` and exited with code 3. That failed the child runbook, and the parent then failed with "Failed to run automation with executionId: c40fd382-… Failed". The failure was in the script's file check. Permissions, the SSM agent and the runbook logic all worked.

**Why the file was missing**
- CloudFormation stack `ssm-m4-r3-a14` launched the instance at 07:17:31 UTC, from launch template `lt-00000000000000023` v1 and image `ami-0000000000000001f`. That was 78 seconds before the script ran. The instance was terminated at 07:21:55.
- The launch request didn't set anything up for `/etc/app/app.conf`, and no step in either runbook creates the file before the check.
- It's not a one-off: every ReleaseOrchestrator run in this region failed the same way (2026-11-14 13:28, and 2026-11-25 at 03:46, 05:34 and 07:18 UTC). The file is never put on the instances this stack builds.

**What I couldn't check**
- The launch template has been deleted, so I couldn't read its startup script to see whether it was meant to create the file.
- The runbook documents and the instance no longer exist either.
- I can't tell whether the file was never set up or the script points at the wrong path.

**Fix:** create `/etc/app/app.conf` when the instance is built (startup script or image), or add a step before `ApplyConfig` that delivers the file or waits for it. Then re-run ReleaseOrchestrator. A separate mitigation plan has been started in the background and will arrive as its own report.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

  - name: WaitForNodeOnline

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### m4 ReleaseOrchestrator fails at ApplyAppConfig
**Description:** ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator runs fail because their child ApplyAppConfig run fails. ApplyConfig step (aws:runCommand → AWS-RunShellScript) exits 3: 'config file /etc/app/app.conf missing'. Failed runs: 2026-11-14 13:28 (a12), 2026-11-25 03:46 (r1), 05:34 (r2), 07:18 (r3) UTC. Account 012345678901_1, us-east-1.
**Time:** 2026-11-14T13:28:55Z

## Findings

### Cause: /etc/app/app.conf absent on target instance i-00000000000000001_47
**Description:** The ApplyConfig step runs a precondition check `if [ ! -f /etc/app/app.conf ]; then exit 3`. On i-00000000000000001_47, command 00000000-0000-4000-8000-9c09aa25f432 returned exit 3. That instance had been launched only ~78s earlier from ami-0000000000000001f by operator-console, and it was terminated at 07:21:55 UTC. This suggests the freshly launched node (AMI or bootstrap) never provisioned /etc/app/app.conf before the release ran. Not yet confirmed.
**Cascades to:** symptom-m4-applyappconfig-failed

#### Supporting Observations
- **Repeated ApplyAppConfig failures: /etc/app/app.conf missing:** Execution history in 012345678901_1 / us-east-1 shows that every ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator run failed because its child ApplyAppConfig run failed. Each run-command exited with code 3: "config file /etc/app/app.conf missing".

- 2026-11-14 13:28 UTC: m4-r3-a12 ApplyAppConfig f7647ed3 (command 9d92d540)
- 2026-11-25 03:46 UTC: m4-r1-a14 orchestrator aebf62ab → ApplyAppConfig 22e9b23e (command 169a15dd)
- 2026-11-25 05:34 UTC: m4-r2-a14 orchestrator cdd22328 → ApplyAppConfig 57004db8 (command dbf3df3b)
- 2026-11-25 07:18 UTC: m4-r3-a14 orchestrator 5f5732bd → ApplyAppConfig c40fd382 (command 34938b01)

The sibling PatchWithSnapshot runs (m5, m5c, m10) all succeeded. Execution 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab does not appear in the list. A DocumentNamePrefix filter of "ReleaseOrchestrator" returned nothing, because the documents are named with an ssm-baseline-… prefix.

### Root Cause: Stack ssm-m4-r3-a14 never puts /etc/app/app.conf on the release node
**Description:** The stack template ([redacted ARN]) defines the Node (EC2, launch template imported from ssm-base-LaunchTemplateId, AL2023 arm64 AMI ami-0000000000000001f), the ApplyAppConfig child runbook and the ReleaseOrchestrator parent. None of these resources writes /etc/app/app.conf, yet ApplyConfig hard-fails (exit 3) when the file is absent. Every ReleaseOrchestrator run in us-east-1 failed this way: Nov 14 13:28, and Nov 25 03:46, 05:34 and 07:18 UTC.
**Cascades to:** hyp-app-conf-missing

#### Gaps
- **Launch template for target instance no longer exists:** Launch template lt-00000000000000023, used to launch i-00000000000000001_47, returns InvalidLaunchTemplateId.NotFound in 012345678901_1/us-east-1. Its UserData and bootstrap cannot be checked to confirm whether /etc/app/app.conf was ever provisioned.
- **Base launch template's startup script can't be inspected:** The ssm-base launch template (lt-00000000000000023) and its exports, the runbook documents and the instance have all been deleted. So it can't be confirmed whether the base startup script was meant to create /etc/app/app.conf, or whether the check uses the wrong path.

## Other Gaps

### No permission to read SSM Automation execution
**Description:** The agent role [redacted ARN] is not authorized to perform ssm:GetAutomationExecution on [redacted ARN], because no identity-based policy allows it. The execution's status, steps and failure details could not be read directly.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Redeploy release stack ssm-m4-r3-a14 with a fixed ApplyAppConfig runbook (adds WaitForNodeOnline and EnsureAppConfig before ApplyConfig), then rerun ReleaseOrchestrator. Durable fix: provision /etc/app/app.conf in the base launch template or AMI.

## Reasoning
Every ReleaseOrchestrator run in 012345678901_1 / us-east-1 (5f5732bd…, aebf62ab…, cdd22328…, child f7647ed3…) fails at ApplyConfig with rc=3 because nothing ever puts /etc/app/app.conf on the node. The ssm-m4-r3-a14 template provisions only the Node, AutomationRole and the two runbooks, and the child runbook went straight to ApplyConfig 78 s after the instance launched. The stack is DELETE_COMPLETE, the ssm-base-* exports and launch template lt-00000000000000023 are gone, and AMI ami-0000000000000001f is a stock Amazon AL2023 image. The fix therefore goes in the runbook now and the base launch template later. The real app.conf contents are unknown and must be supplied (AppConfigBase64). The plan passed the safety policy check; nothing has been executed.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Prepare

#### 1.1 Capture the last deployed stack configuration as the rollback baseline
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --region us-east-1 --stack-name [redacted ARN] > stack-baseline.json
```
**Purpose:** Capture the last deployed stack configuration as the rollback baseline.
**Advisory:** Check that this backup covers the stack, both SSM documents, the IAM role and the node.

#### 1.2 Back up the original template and create a working copy
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation get-template --region us-east-1 --stack-name [redacted ARN] --template-stage Original --query TemplateBody --output text > release-original.yaml && cp release-original.yaml release-fixed.yaml
```
**Purpose:** Back up the original template and create a working copy.

#### 1.3 Add a readiness wait and a config-delivery step so ApplyConfig's…
**Type:** command
```
# ChildRunbook.Properties.Content
parameters:
  AppConfigBase64: {type: String, description: 'base64 of the desired /etc/app/app.conf'}
mainSteps:  # insert BEFORE ApplyConfig
  - name: WaitForNodeOnline
    action: aws:waitForAwsResourceProperty
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    inputs:
      Service: ssm
      Api: DescribeInstanceInformation
      InstanceInformationFilterList:
        - key: InstanceIds
          valueSet: ['{{ InstanceId }}']
      PropertySelector: '$.InstanceInformationList[0].PingStatus'
      DesiredValues: [Online]
  - name: EnsureAppConfig
    action: aws:runCommand
    timeoutSeconds: 600
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{ InstanceId }}']
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - cloud-init status --wait || true
          - mkdir -p /etc/app
          - if [ ! -f /etc/app/app.conf ]; then echo '{{ AppConfigBase64 }}' | base64 -d > /etc/app/app.conf && chmod 0644 /etc/app/app.conf; fi
          - test -s /etc/app/app.conf
# ParentRunbook: add the AppConfigBase64 parameter and pass it via
# RunApplyConfig.inputs.RuntimeParameters.AppConfigBase64: ['{{ AppConfigBase64 }}']
```
**Purpose:** Add a readiness wait and a config-delivery step so ApplyConfig's precondition is always met. The existing AutomationRole already permits both, so no IAM change is needed.
**Risks:** The real app.conf contents are unknown. The application owner must supply them, because a placeholder file would let ApplyConfig pass with the app misconfigured.
**Advisory:** 'cloud-init status --wait' covers the case where user data writes the file but hadn't finished (the node was only 78 s old).

### Step 2: Pre Validate

#### 2.1 Confirm the ssm-base-* exports exist
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation list-exports --region us-east-1 --query "Exports[?starts_with(Name,'ssm-base-')].[Name,Value]" --output table
```
**Purpose:** Confirm the ssm-base-* exports exist. They are currently absent, so redeploy the ssm-base stack first.
**Risks:** Stack creation fails with 'No export named ssm-base-...' if the base stack is not redeployed.

#### 2.2 Check whether the base launch template's user data creates…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --region us-east-1 --launch-template-id <ssm-base-LaunchTemplateId> --versions <ssm-base-LaunchTemplateVersion> --query 'LaunchTemplateVersions[0].LaunchTemplateData.UserData' --output text | base64 -d
```
**Purpose:** Check whether the base launch template's user data creates /etc/app/app.conf.

#### 2.3 Validate the edited template's syntax before deploying
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation validate-template --region us-east-1 --template-body file://release-fixed.yaml
```
**Purpose:** Validate the edited template's syntax before deploying.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Redeploy the stack with the fixed runbooks
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation create-stack --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m4-r3-a14 --template-body file://release-fixed.yaml --parameters ParameterKey=RunTag,ParameterValue=m4-r3-a14 --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM --tags Key=Project,Value=devops-agent-skills-test Key=DevOpsAgentManaged,Value=true Key=auto-delete,Value=no && aws cloudformation wait stack-create-complete --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m4-r3-a14
```
**Purpose:** Redeploy the stack with the fixed runbooks.
**Risks:** Launches a new EC2 instance, which costs money while it runs.

### Step 4: Post Validate

#### 4.1 Confirm CREATE_COMPLETE and record the new Node instance ID
**Type:** command
```
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m4-r3-a14 --query 'Stacks[0].[StackStatus,Outputs]'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm CREATE_COMPLETE and record the new Node instance ID.

#### 4.2 Rerun ReleaseOrchestrator and poll until it reaches Success
**Type:** command
```
EXEC=$(aws ssm start-automation-execution --region us-east-1 --document-name ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14-ReleaseOrchestrator --parameters InstanceId=<Node output>,AutomationAssumeRole=[redacted ARN],AppConfigBase64=<base64 of app.conf> --query AutomationExecutionId --output text); aws ssm get-automation-execution --region us-east-1 --automation-execution-id $EXEC --query 'AutomationExecution.AutomationExecutionStatus'
```
**Purpose:** Rerun ReleaseOrchestrator and poll until it reaches Success.
**Advisory:** In the child run, confirm WaitForNodeOnline, EnsureAppConfig and ApplyConfig all succeed and that the output contains 'configuration applied'.

### Step 5: Rollback

#### 5.1 Return to the current state (stack absent) once no automations are in…
**Type:** command
```
aws ssm describe-automation-executions --region us-east-1 --filters Key=DocumentNamePrefix,Values=ssm-baseline-m4-r3-a14 Key=ExecutionStatus,Values=InProgress && aws cloudformation delete-stack --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m4-r3-a14 && aws cloudformation wait stack-delete-complete --region us-east-1 --stack-name ssm-m4-r3-a14
```
**Purpose:** Return to the current state (stack absent) once no automations are in progress.
**Risks:** Terminates the node and removes both runbooks and the automation role.
**Advisory:** Alternatively, redeploy release-original.yaml to restore the original runbooks.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Make the ApplyAppConfig runbook check its precondition and wait for the node to be ready before ApplyConfig.
**Description:** Make WaitForNodeOnline, EnsureAppConfig (or an equivalent config-delivery step) and the AppConfigBase64 pass-through permanent in the ssm-m4-r3-a14 source template (ChildRunbook and ParentRunbook). Keep ApplyConfig's existing check as a final safety check.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A fresh deployment followed by an immediate ReleaseOrchestrator run succeeds, with no 'config file /etc/app/app.conf missing' error.
- The runbook waits for SSM PingStatus=Online and for cloud-init to finish before ApplyConfig.

#### 2. Provision /etc/app/app.conf at instance launch.
**Description:** Update the ssm-base launch template's user data to write /etc/app/app.conf (e.g. cloud-init write_files), or bake it into a custom AMI built from al2023 (ami-0000000000000001f). Then publish a new version and update the ssm-base-LaunchTemplateVersion export.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A newly launched node has a non-empty /etc/app/app.conf as soon as cloud-init finishes.
- The ssm-base-* exports exist and point to the new launch template version.
